heading: Operation of unauthorized unmanned aircraft over wildfires

tree.heading: In General.—
tree.text: Except as provided in subsection (b), an individual who operates an unmanned aircraft and knowingly or recklessly interferes with a wildfire suppression, or law enforcement or emergency response efforts 1 related to a wildfire suppression, shall be fined under this title, imprisoned for not more than 2 years, or both.

tree.heading: Exceptions.—
tree.text: This section does not apply to the operation of an unmanned aircraft conducted by a unit or agency of the United States Government or of a State, tribal, or local government (including any individual conducting such operation pursuant to a contract or other agreement entered into with the unit or agency) for the purpose of protecting the public safety and welfare, including firefighting, law enforcement, or emergency response.

tree.heading: Definitions.—
tree.text: In this section, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Unmanned aircraft.—
children.text: The term “unmanned aircraft” has the meaning given the term in section 44801 of title 49, United States Code.

children.heading: Wildfire.—
children.text: The term “wildfire” has the meaning given that term in section 2 of the Emergency Wildfire Suppression Act (42 U.S.C. 1856m).

children.heading: Wildfire suppression.—
children.text: The term “wildfire suppression” means an effort to contain, extinguish, or suppress a wildfire.

sourceCredit: (Added Pub. L. 115–254, div. B, title III, § 382(a), Oct. 5, 2018, 132 Stat. 3320.)
